gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the makers' UPS promise covers only the AC outlets. EcoFlow's US RIVER 3 Plus page says 'All three AC outlets have UPS protection' and says nothing about the USB or car ports. BLUETTI's Elite 30 V2 page gives '≤10ms' and '980W bypass' without naming any outputs. So the shopper who saves energy by running the router from USB or 12 V gets no written switchover promise from the maker for that port.
standout_why: I compared four pages. outagemath.com (cited) says only that 'a station with UPS or EPS mode keeps the internet on without a blip' and tells you to check the switchover time. It says nothing about which ports the UPS covers. wattpowerstation.com (cited) has no UPS, pass-through or auto-off content at all; its only DC figure is Hobotech's DELTA Pro 3 idle draw. Our own dealectric page gives switchover times per model but does not say whether those times apply to the DC or USB ports. None of the ChatGPT answers raise the conflict between running on DC and having UPS switchover. They also don't mention Anker's 15 W cap on the C300 DC's USB-C4 port.
decides: This narrows the pick rather than overturning it. If the router must survive a power cut with no blip, the only route the makers document is AC with UPS on, which gives up the DC savings. If the shopper goes DC-only to lose the least power, which is question pm015, they should treat the station as a battery they switch over to by hand, or test the DC port themselves, until the maker confirms DC pass-through. On the Anker SOLIX C300 DC, a 12 V router needs one of the 140 W ports (USB-C1 to C3). USB-C4 is limited to 15 W and shares 20 W with USB-A.
